title:
The Death of the
Rice Farmer
description: Birds keep eating a farmer's rice. He lies still in his field and uses a surprising trick to protect his harvest.

source.adaptation: Original Hypa retelling of the documented folktale; see SOURCES.md.

lines.text: A farmer once planted a field of rice.
He cleared the ground, pulled the weeds, and tended the plants, looking forward to his harvest.
But birds discovered the field.
Every day they flew down and ate the rice.
“Leave my crop alone!” the farmer shouted.
He ran among the plants, waving his arms.
The birds scattered, but whenever he left, they returned.
Soon he was spending more time chasing birds than caring for his farm.
He grew tired, and still his rice disappeared.
One afternoon, he stopped shouting and watched them.
When he moved towards them, they flew away.
When he stood at a distance, they waited.
The moment they thought he was gone, they settled in the field again.
The farmer thought for a long time.
Then he made a plan.
He killed an animal and took out its entrails.
Carrying them to the field, he lay down among the rice and placed them across his belly.
To anyone watching, it looked as though he had died.
Then he lay perfectly still.
ask: Why does the farmer pretend to be dead?

lines.text: The birds appeared, but they did not come close at first.
This was the same man who always chased them.
They watched him.
The farmer did not move.
One bird landed nearby.
Another followed.
They waited for the familiar shout, but the field remained quiet.
The farmer could hear their wings and their feet moving among the plants.
Still, he waited.
The birds grew bolder.
Believing the farmer was dead, they gathered closer, until they were within his reach.
Suddenly, he sprang up.
ask: How does the farmer protect his field?

lines.text: Before they could escape, he caught them.
The man they had believed was dead was alive, and his trick had succeeded.
From that day, those birds no longer troubled his field.
The farmer could tend his rice without spending every hour chasing them away.
When harvest came, his work had not been wasted.
And that is why this tale is called The Death of the Rice Farmer.
The farmer did not die.
He stopped repeating what had failed, studied his problem, and found another way to protect his crop.
